questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of living things?
questions.explanation: Combustion is the rapid burning of a fuel in oxygen at high temperature; it is a chemical process, not a life process. Living cells release energy from food by respiration, which is gradual, enzyme-controlled and happens at body temperature.

distractorRationale.a: Respiration occurs in every living cell and releases energy from food
distractorRationale.b: Irritability is the ability to detect and respond to a stimulus
distractorRationale.d: Excretion removes the waste products of metabolism

questions.stem: A young shoot bends towards a window over several days. This behaviour illustrates which characteristic of living things?
questions.explanation: Light is the stimulus and bending is the response, so the shoot is showing irritability, in this case as the growth movement called phototropism. It also involves movement of parts, but the key idea being tested is the detection of and response to a stimulus.

distractorRationale.a: Nutrition is making or taking in food, which is a separate process from bending
distractorRationale.c: No waste product is being removed
distractorRationale.d: No new individual is being produced

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes excretion from egestion?

options.text: Excretion removes undigested food; egestion removes urea
Excretion removes waste made by the body's own reactions; egestion removes undigested food
Both remove undigested food, but by different openings
Excretion occurs only in plants and egestion only in animals

questions.explanation: Excretory products such as urea, carbon dioxide and excess salts are made inside cells during metabolism and must be removed because they are toxic if they accumulate. Faeces, by contrast, is material that was never absorbed into the cells at all, so removing it is egestion, not excretion.

distractorRationale.a: The two definitions have been swapped
distractorRationale.c: Excretion has nothing to do with undigested food
distractorRationale.d: Plants excrete too, for example oxygen and tannins, and animals do both

questions.stem: A crystal placed in a saturated solution increases in size. Why is this not regarded as growth in the biological sense?

options.text: Because the crystal does not change size at all
Because material is added only on the outside and there is no increase in complexity or living tissue
Because growth must always be visible to the naked eye
Because crystals are found only in laboratories

questions.explanation: Biological growth is an irreversible increase in dry mass and in complexity, produced from within by cell division and the making of new protoplasm. A crystal merely accretes identical particles onto its surface, and it neither respires, excretes nor reproduces.

distractorRationale.a: The crystal genuinely does enlarge; the issue is the manner of enlargement
distractorRationale.c: Much biological growth, such as that of bacteria, is invisible to the naked eye
distractorRationale.d: Crystals such as salt and quartz form naturally; where they form is irrelevant

questions.stem: Which single feature of viruses makes biologists reluctant to classify them as fully living organisms?

options.text: They are too small to be seen with a light microscope
They can only reproduce inside a living host cell and carry out no metabolism of their own
They cause diseases in plants and animals

questions.explanation: A virus has no cytoplasm, no organelles and no enzymes, so it cannot respire, feed, grow or excrete. Reproduction is the only life process it shows, and even that depends entirely on hijacking the machinery of a host cell.

distractorRationale.a: Bacteria are visible under a light microscope and many organisms are microscopic; size is not the issue
distractorRationale.c: All living things contain nucleic acid, so this would argue that viruses are living
distractorRationale.d: Many undisputedly living organisms, such as Plasmodium and bacteria, also cause disease

questions.stem: The release of energy from food within living cells is known as
questions.explanation: Respiration is the enzyme-controlled breakdown of food, usually glucose, to release energy for the cell's work. It happens in every living cell continuously, whether or not the organism has lungs.

distractorRationale.a: Nutrition supplies the food; it does not release the energy from it
distractorRationale.c: Breathing is only the physical movement of air into and out of the lungs
distractorRationale.d: Assimilation is the use of absorbed food to build new protoplasm

questions.stem: A dry plank of iroko wood should be described as non-living rather than dead.
questions.explanation: False. The plank was once part of a living tree that respired, grew and reproduced, so it is dead. Non-living describes something that never carried out life processes at all, such as a stone or a plastic bucket.

questions.stem: Movement in plants differs from movement in most animals mainly because plant movement

options.text: involves growth of parts rather than locomotion of the whole organism
is caused by wind rather than by the plant

questions.explanation: Plants are anchored by roots, so they cannot move from place to place. Instead they respond to stimuli by growing unevenly — shoots bend towards light and roots grow downwards — and these growth movements are called tropisms.

distractorRationale.a: Plants do move; tropisms and the opening of stomata are genuine movements
distractorRationale.c: All movement in living things uses energy from respiration
distractorRationale.d: Being blown by wind is passive and is not the plant's own movement

questions.stem: A student argues that a motor car is a living thing because it takes in fuel, gives out exhaust gas, moves and responds when the key is turned. Give three reasons why the car is not living.
markingGuide: The car cannot reproduce — it cannot produce another car of its own kind (2 marks)
The car cannot grow — it does not increase in size, dry mass or complexity from within (2 marks)
The car does not respire — energy is released by combustion of fuel at high temperature, not by enzyme-controlled respiration inside cells (2 marks)
Accept also: it is not made of cells; it cannot respond without an external operator; it does not excrete metabolic waste from its own reactions (1 mark each, to the maximum)
questions.explanation: A convincing answer identifies life processes the car genuinely lacks rather than repeating the ones the student listed. Reproduction, growth, cellular respiration and being made of cells are the strongest points, because the car fails each of them absolutely.

questions.stem: Which of these observations is the best single piece of evidence that a sealed sachet of dried yeast contains living organisms?

options.text: When mixed with warm sugar solution, gas bubbles are produced and the mixture froths
The powder feels dry to the touch
The sachet has an expiry date printed on it

questions.explanation: Frothing shows that carbon dioxide is being produced, which means the yeast is respiring anaerobically on the sugar. Respiration is a life process, and gas production that depends on warmth and food is strong evidence of living cells.

distractorRationale.a: Colour is a physical property shared by many non-living powders
distractorRationale.c: Being dry says nothing about whether the cells are alive; dormant cells are dry
distractorRationale.d: A printed date is information from the manufacturer, not biological evidence
